answer: Cap Sybil farms with a regenerating action budget: each identity gets daily credits refilling slowly, one per day, and each action spends one. A user who wanders through the system a few times a day never notices the ledge, but a farm running thousands of accounts hits the ceiling at once: its plume of fake activity collapses, because credits cannot be bought, transferred, or minted on demand. Unused credits decay after weeks, so hoarded accounts lose value, and bursts trigger a freezing cooldown. Attackers must wait months to build influence or pay dearly for aged accounts.
